 WTA Hong Kong Day 3 Predictions Including Maya Joint vs Maria Sakkari 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 WTA Hong Kong ‘s third day is well and truly upon us, with a mix of first-round and second-round singles action headlined by a blockbuster between Leylah Fernandez and Sofia Kenin. With late-season ranking points on the line and danger lurking at every turn, as ever, we here at LWOT will be offering our predictions for every match, but who will advance?
 WTA Hong Kong Day 3 Predictions
 Antonia Ruzic vs Alina Charaeva
 Head-to-Head: first meeting
 Ruzic and Charaeva meet for the first time in an official WTA main draw, with their only previous encounter coming at an ITF event in Slovenia in 2023, which does not count towards the head-to-head record used here. Ruzic will look to make the most of her experience at tour level, while Charaeva has an opportunity to cause an upset and make a statement against a higher-ranked opponent.
 Ruzic’s greater exposure to this level of competition gives her an edge, particularly if she can dictate play from the baseline and avoid giving Charaeva opportunities to settle. The Croatian should have enough quality to navigate the challenge, although her opponent could make her work for it.
 Prediction: Ruzic in 2
 Leylah Fernandez vs Sofia Kenin
 Head-to-Head: First meeting
 Fernandez begins her Hong Kong campaign against a former Grand Slam champion, with Kenin presenting a potentially awkward opening test. The Canadian arrives as the No. 3 seed and will look to use her consistency and ability to redirect pace to control the rallies. Kenin, meanwhile, has the experience and variety to disrupt that rhythm, particularly if she can take the ball early and prevent Fernandez from settling into exchanges.
 Tennis – U.S. Open – Flushing Meadows, New York, United States – September 4, 2026 Canada’s Leylah Fernandez in action during her third round match against Jessica Pegula of the U.S. REUTERS/Jeenah Moon TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY 
 There is little separating the pair in terms of their ability to construct points, but Fernandez’s defensive coverage and greater consistency give her a slight advantage. Kenin can make this competitive, although the Canadian should have enough to come through her first test.
 Prediction: Fernandez in 2
 Claire Liu vs Katie Boulter
 Head-to-Head: First meeting
 Liu and Boulter both made encouraging starts to their campaigns, advancing in straight sets. Liu defeated Tatiana Prozorova 6–2 6–4, while Boulter was equally convincing against Viktorija Golubic, winning 6–2 7–6. The Briton will be looking to build on that performance as she begins her second-round challenge.
 Liu is a capable hard-court player and has the consistency to make Boulter work for every point. However, Boulter’s more aggressive approach should allow her to dictate the tempo if she serves well and takes her chances when returning. Liu is unlikely to make this straightforward, but Boulter has the weapons to come through.
 Prediction: Boulter in 2
 Talia Gibson vs Aliaksandra Sasnovich
 Head-to-Head: Sasnovich 2–0 Gibson
 Gibson faces a familiar opponent in Sasnovich, who has won both of their previous meetings, including a straight-sets victory in Beijing earlier this year. The Australian will take confidence from her opening-round win over Oleksandra Oliynykova, while Sasnovich also arrives with momentum after defeating Katie Volynets 6–3 6–2.
 The head-to-head gives Sasnovich a psychological advantage, but Gibson’s recent progress and higher level on the tour make this a different proposition. The Australian has the power to take control of rallies, although she will need to manage Sasnovich’s consistency and ability to extend points. Expect a much closer contest than their previous meetings, with Gibson having enough firepower to turn the rivalry around.
 Prediction: Gibson in 3
 Maya Joint vs Maria Sakkari
 Head-to-Head: First meeting
 Maria Sakkari defeated Carol Young Suh Lee 6–1 6–4, while Joint followed up a competitive first set against Maddison Inglis to claim a 7–5 6–2 win. The Greek will be keen to build momentum as the No. 4 seed, but Joint has shown that she can handle the demands of the main tour.
 Sakkari’s athleticism and ability to sustain a high level of intensity should make her difficult to overcome. Joint has the confidence to challenge her, particularly if she can use her forehand to move Sakkari around the court. However, the Greek’s experience in these situations could prove decisive, especially in the important moments.
 Prediction: Sakkari in 2
